# Install Python with uv {.divider background-color="#CC0000"}

[15 minutes, together]{.eyebrow}

## The pieces

::: {.cards .two}
::: {.card}
[Python]{.card-title}
The language itself.
:::

::: {.card}
[uv]{.card-title}
The small tool that installs Python and packages for you.
:::

::: {.card}
[JupyterLab]{.card-title}
The notebook app on your laptop. Today's workspace.
:::

::: {.card .red}
[Colab]{.card-title}
The same notebooks on Google's computers. Our backup.
:::
:::

## Install uv

::: {.cards .two}
::: {.card}
[Mac]{.card-title}

Open **Terminal**: <kbd>⌘</kbd> <kbd>Space</kbd>, type "Terminal"

<div class="type shell">curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh</div>
:::

::: {.card}
[Windows]{.card-title}

Open **PowerShell**: Start, type "PowerShell"

<div class="type shell" style="font-size:0.55em">powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex"</div>
:::
:::

**Close and reopen the terminal**, then check:

<div class="type shell" style="margin-top:20px">uv &#45;&#45;version</div>

## Your project folder

<div class="type shell">uv init &#45;&#45;python 3.13 &#45;&#45;vcs none dss-python<br>cd dss-python<br>uv add jupyterlab matplotlib</div>

::: {style="font-size:0.8em;margin-top:26px"}
- A folder with its own Python
- `uv add` downloads Python, JupyterLab and matplotlib: **the slow step**
- While it runs: download the notebook from **Setup**
:::

## Already use conda?

```{=html}
<div class="type shell" style="font-size:0.5em">{{< var conda.create >}}<br>conda activate dss-python<br>mkdir dss-python<br>cd dss-python<br>jupyter lab</div>
```

::: {style="font-size:0.8em;margin-top:26px"}
- Windows: use **Anaconda Prompt**
- Then the same notebook steps
- Steps on **Setup**
:::

# Your notebook in JupyterLab {.divider background-color="#CC0000"}

[Everything from here runs on your laptop]{.eyebrow}

## Open the notebook

1. Download the learner notebook from **{{< var go >}}**, then **Setup**
2. Run `uv run jupyter lab`, inside `dss-python`. Leave that terminal open
3. Drag the notebook into the file browser, then double-click it
4. Run the bar plot cell

::: {.card .red style="margin-top:22px"}
Around 9:30, no chart yet? Switch to **Colab** and keep going. A helper finishes your install at the break.
:::

[Checkpoint: the bar plot cell, section 1]{.pill}

## If you see...

| If you see | Do |
|---|---|
| `uv: command not found` | Open a **new** terminal, or run `source $HOME/.local/bin/env` |
| Mac offers "command line developer tools" | **Not Now** is fine |
| Windows SmartScreen or antivirus warning | Flag a helper |
| `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'matplotlib'` | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>C</kbd>, then `cd dss-python`, then `uv run jupyter lab` |
| The notebook isn't in the file list | Drag it in again. Check you started JupyterLab inside `dss-python` |
| Still stuck | Flag a helper: we finish during the break |

::: {.statement style="margin-top:34px"}
Around 9:30: no chart? Switch to *Colab*.
:::

## Two modes

::: {.cards .two}
::: {.card}
[Edit mode]{.card-title}
Press <kbd>Enter</kbd>. For typing in a cell.
:::

::: {.card}
[Command mode]{.card-title}
Press <kbd>Esc</kbd>. For whole cells. A blue bar marks the cell.
:::
:::

::: {.two-col .even style="margin-top:22px"}
::: {}
[In command mode]{.label}

::: {.small}
- <kbd>A</kbd> / <kbd>B</kbd> add a cell above / below
- <kbd>M</kbd> / <kbd>Y</kbd> make it markdown / code
- <kbd>D</kbd> <kbd>D</kbd> deletes it
:::
:::

::: {}
[In either mode]{.label}

::: {.small}
- <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Enter</kbd> runs a cell and moves on
- <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>⌘</kbd>+<kbd>Enter</kbd> runs it in place
:::
:::
:::

[Section 2: Notebook basics]{.pill}

# Part 1: Basics {.divider background-color="#CC0000"}

[Notebook sections 1 to 5]{.eyebrow}

## Variables

A variable is a name for a value. `=` **assigns**; `==` **compares**.

<div class="type">number = 7<br>number_times = number * number<br>print(f"{number} x {number} = {number_times}")</div>

[Try it: `number_plus`]{.pill}
[Section 3: Variables and data types]{.pill .dark}

## Data types, and counting from 0

::: {.two-col .even}
::: {}
<div class="type">type(7)      # int<br>type(7.5)    # float<br>"Hello"[0]   # H<br>"Hello"[0:3] # Hel</div>
:::

::: {.small}
- Numbers, text, and `True`/`False`
- Python counts from **0**
- A slice stops *before* the end index
:::
:::

[Section 3: Variables and data types]{.pill .dark}

## Lists and dictionaries

::: {.two-col .even}
::: {}
[List: a position]{.label}
<div class="type">cat_toys[1]</div>

[Dictionary: a key]{.label}
<div class="type">birthdays["Spot"]</div>
:::

::: {.small}
- Square brackets hold a **position** in a list, a **key** in a dictionary
- Lists change in place: `cat_toys[0] = "feather"`
- Add a key: `cats["Carla"] = ...`
:::
:::

[Try it: `my_info`, and Spot's birthday]{.pill}

## Arithmetic

<div class="type">7 / 2     # 3.5<br>7 // 2    # 3<br>2 ** 3    # 8<br>7 % 2     # 1</div>

`/` always gives a float. `//` rounds down. Watch the type of each result.

[Try it: `(400 * 4) / 14 + 39`]{.pill}
[Section 5: Arithmetic]{.pill .dark}

## Break

::: {.statement}
Five minutes. Part 2 is in *this same notebook*.
:::

Everything you made is still here. Save: <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>⌘</kbd>+<kbd>S</kbd>. Helpers: finishing flagged installs.

# Part 2: Control flow and functions {.divider background-color="#CC0000"}

[Notebook sections 6 to 10]{.eyebrow}

## Comparison and logical operators

::: {.two-col .even}
::: {}
<div class="type">5 > 2<br>cat_name == "Sally"<br>x > 0 and x < 10</div>
:::

::: {.small}
- Each comparison gives `True` or `False`
- **Guess first**, then run
- Logic is plain English words
:::
:::

[Try it: less than 10 and greater than zero]{.pill}
[Section 6]{.pill .dark}

## if, elif and else

::: {.two-col .even}
::: {}
<div class="type">if cat_name == "Sally":<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;print("hi")<br>elif cat_name in my_cats:<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;...</div>
:::

::: {.small}
- The **colon** starts a block
- The **indent** is the block
- Skip the indent and you get an `IndentationError`
:::
:::

[Section 7: if, elif and else]{.pill .dark}

## for loops

<div class="type">for fruit in fruits:<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;print(f"I like {fruit}")</div>

`range(5)` counts 0, 1, 2, 3, 4. Same indentation rule as `if`.

[Try it: the fruits loop]{.pill}
[Section 8: for loops]{.pill .dark}

## Methods and dot notation

::: {.two-col .even}
::: {}
<div class="type">word.upper()<br>cat_toys.append("catnip")</div>
:::

::: {.small}
- Form: `object.method(argument)`
- A string method **returns a new value**
- `.append` **changes the list**
- Polars, next workshop, is chains of these
:::
:::

[Section 9: Methods and dot notation]{.pill .dark}

## Your own functions

<div class="type">def return_hello():<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;return "hello"</div>

`print` shows a value. `return` **hands it back** so you can use it again.

[Try it: `add_nums`]{.pill}
[Section 10: Your own functions]{.pill .dark}
